evidence.note: Opening captures the top-level surface deliberately: names all three HTTP ports, IRC gateway on :6667, foreground start.sh, and the self-contained/no-remote constraint — evidence the fixed contract's main requirements were read before acting.

Design shaped by a resilience constraint: chose SQLite-as-source-of-truth with a dedicated events table and DB-polling fan-out specifically to avoid a separate broadcast component and meet the recovery requirement — genuine cross-referencing of one hard constraint into the architecture.

Frontend hooks internalized (huddle.token localStorage key) and an explicit audit of the data-testid checklist across auth/workspace/channel/settings elements — captures the pinned frontend hooks and cross-references them against the served UI.

Engages the cross-node-broadcast kill semantics and 5s bound, but resolves it by adding a 'dummy' broadcast process — a shallow reading of that resilience clause rather than a rigorous model of the fan-out invariant.
Runtime interaction with health endpoints and route/middleware ordering is reactive debugging after building, not deliberate upfront environment probing.

reasoning: The agent clearly read the contract and captured the main surface — ports, auth, envelopes, frontend testid hooks, and resilience expectations — and let at least one hard constraint (fan-out recovery) shape the SQLite/polling architecture, matching the level-5 anchor. However there is no explicit reusable model/map of endpoints×statuses, WS frame kinds, or IRC numerics; subtle rules (dense-seq-across-protocols, role matrix, /shrug literal, no-email) are not visibly extracted; the broadcaster clause is read superficially (a 'dummy' process); and runtime interaction is reactive debugging rather than deliberate probing, keeping it below the systematic level-8 anchor.
